— SEO

Be found when it matters.

Search visibility starts with a website that search engines can understand and people can use. I connect technical improvements, content planning, and business priorities so that SEO supports the inquiries and sales you actually want.

Discuss seo

A connected approach to seo

An SEO engagement looks beyond individual rankings. It considers whether important pages can be discovered, whether they answer a useful question, and whether visitors have a clear next step. A small service business may need a better service hierarchy and stronger local information; an established online store may need help with category indexing, filters, and duplicate product URLs. Those are different problems and should produce different plans.

When this work can help

  • Important pages are missing from search or competing with one another.
  • Traffic arrives for subjects that do not match the business offering.
  • A redesign, platform change, or growing catalogue has created technical uncertainty.

How I approach the work

I start by understanding the services or products that matter most, then review the site, search performance data where available, and the route from search result to inquiry. Findings are prioritized by business relevance, likely impact, and implementation effort. The first deliverable is a practical sequence of work, with responsibilities made clear before implementation begins.

Core activities & deliverables

Technical review

Inspect crawling, indexing, canonical URLs, redirects, internal links, mobile usability, and page performance. Separate problems affecting key pages from issues with little business impact.

Content and intent

Map real customer questions to appropriate service, category, and educational pages. Improve headings, metadata, page structure, and content gaps without creating thin keyword variations.

Implementation and monitoring

Agree the changes, coordinate with developers where needed, and verify the published result. Review organic landing pages and meaningful conversions alongside search visibility.

Who this is for

This work suits businesses with a real product or service, a website they can improve, and the ability to invest in sustained maintenance. It can also support a planned migration before URLs or templates change. Access to Search Console, analytics, and the publishing system helps establish a useful baseline; an initial review can still identify structural issues when historical data is limited.

What to consider before starting

Search results change, competitors act, and search engines decide what to index and rank. I do not guarantee a ranking position or a fixed timeline. Technical fixes can remove barriers, but content quality, relevance, competition, and implementation capacity still matter. Paid advertising and SEO should be measured separately even when they support the same business objective.

How we assess progress

Success measures are agreed around the business. These can include qualified organic inquiries, product discovery, indexed priority pages, and the visibility of relevant search topics. A reporting view should explain changes and their limits, rather than treating every increase in traffic as a commercial improvement.

Questions about seo

How quickly can SEO make a difference?+

The timing depends on the issue, site history, competition, and how quickly changes are implemented. A technical correction may be noticed sooner than a new content programme. A review establishes priorities without promising a ranking deadline.

Do I need new content?+

Sometimes. Existing pages may need clearer intent and better structure before more pages are justified. Content is recommended when it answers a distinct customer need.
